split_rule: Split fixed before any retrieval run. Test = 5 questions, mostly on Functions sections 6.3-6.6 (dev touches chapter 6 only via 6.1-6.2) plus 2 chapter-filter questions on topics not used in dev. Leakage risk: same book and writing style for dev and test.
selection_rule: Choose the strategy on DEV only: highest Evidence Hit@3; tie -> higher Hit@1; tie -> fewer chunks. Test is reported once after the choice is fixed.

questions.question: Which values does bool() convert to False?
questions.expected_answer: 0 and the empty string
questions.evidence_quote: False: 0, empty string

questions.question: How many comparison operators does Python have?
questions.evidence_quote: The 6 comparison operators:

questions.question: What goes wrong if I write is_zero = num=0 to check whether num is zero?
questions.expected_answer: It assigns 0 to both is_zero and num; = is assignment, == is comparison
questions.evidence_quote: is_zero = num=0 will always assign is_zero and num with 0, regardless of num's original value.

questions.question: How many spaces per indentation level does PEP 8 recommend?
questions.expected_answer: Four spaces
questions.evidence_quote: The PEP 8 style guide recommends four spaces per indentation level.

questions.question: Which operator is the exception to left associativity in Python?
questions.expected_answer: Exponentiation (**) is right associative
questions.evidence_quote: Exponentiation is the main exception (noted above) and is right associative

questions.question: Why not just use two separate if statements instead of elif when only one branch should run?
questions.expected_answer: Separate ifs do not guarantee only one branch runs; both may execute
questions.evidence_quote: Two separate if statements do not guarantee that only one branch is taken and might result in both branches being taken.

questions.question: What is another name for a conditional expression?
questions.expected_answer: Ternary operator
questions.evidence_quote: also known as a "ternary operator"

questions.question: What precedence does a conditional expression have compared to other operations?
questions.expected_answer: The lowest precedence of all Python operations
questions.evidence_quote: Conditional expressions have the lowest precedence of all Python operations.

questions.question: Is the end value included in the sequence produced by range()?
questions.expected_answer: No; inclusive of start, exclusive of end
questions.evidence_quote: This integer sequence is inclusive of the start and exclusive of the end of the sequence.

questions.question: What is a loop that never stops on its own called?
questions.expected_answer: An infinite loop (a loop without a termination condition)
questions.evidence_quote: A loop without a termination condition is known as an infinite loop.

questions.question: After a continue statement executes, what happens next in the loop?
questions.expected_answer: The loop expression is evaluated again and the loop continues from it
questions.evidence_quote: After the continue statement's execution, the loop expression will be evaluated again

questions.question: When is a for loop preferable to a while loop in nested loops?
questions.expected_answer: When counting with range() or iterating over a container object
questions.evidence_quote: A for loop is a preferable option in cases where a loop is used for counting purposes using a range() function

questions.question: In this chapter, when does the else statement run?
questions.expected_answer: After the loop finishes without being interrupted by a break
questions.evidence_quote: A loop else statement runs after the loop's execution is completed without being interrupted by a break

alt_gold.evidence_quote: A loop else is used to identify if the loop is terminated normally or the execution is interrupted by a break statement.

questions.question: In this chapter, how is nesting indicated?
questions.expected_answer: By an indentation level (a decision statement inside another decision statement)
questions.evidence_quote: Nesting allows a decision statement to be inside another decision statement, and is indicated by an indentation level.

questions.question: In this chapter, what does control flow mean?
questions.expected_answer: The sequence of program execution
questions.evidence_quote: Control flow is the sequence of program execution.

questions.question: What is the difference between a function argument and a function parameter?
questions.expected_answer: An argument is the value passed in a call; a parameter is the variable for that input in the definition
questions.evidence_quote: A function argument is a value passed as input during a function call. A function parameter is a variable representing the input in the function definition.

questions.question: Why should a list not be used as a default parameter value?
questions.expected_answer: Default values are defined only once, so mutable objects like lists should not be defaults
questions.evidence_quote: Default parameter values are only defined once to be used by the function, so mutable objects (such as lists) should not be used as default values.

questions.question: How can code inside a function change the value of a variable defined outside it?
questions.expected_answer: Declare it with the global keyword inside the function
questions.evidence_quote: To edit a global variable inside a function, the variable must be declared with the global keyword.

questions.question: In this chapter, what does the outer one control when one is placed inside another?
questions.expected_answer: The outer loop controls how many times the inner loop fully executes
questions.evidence_quote: The outer loop controls the number of the inner loop's full execution.

questions.question: In this chapter, what is a branch?
questions.expected_answer: A group of statements that execute based on a condition
questions.evidence_quote: A branch is a group of statements that execute based on a condition.
